info.title: GSM Supplier API: internal reference
info.description:
Every route of the API: admin console, merchant portal, storefront, REST API v1, Dhru Fusion, incoming webhooks and system routes. Generated from the route contracts; the public subset is `/openapi.json`.

Each operation shows its access kind (`x-gsm-access`), the permission a staff route, or the scope an API key, needs (`x-gsm-permission`) and the manifest key (`x-gsm-key`).

**Conventions.** JSON bodies use camelCase names. Money is a string with exactly four decimals (`"12.4900"`), timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`"2026-03-01T09:30:00.000Z"`) and ids are numbers. Errors are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`; quote the `requestId` when you contact support.

get.description: Newest first. `actorType` is staff, client, customer or system (system rows have no `actorId`, `actorName` or `ip`; the console shows "System"). `actorName` and `entityLabel` are snapshots written with the entry, so renamed or deleted records still read correctly. `entityType` is a word of the closed list `AUDIT_ENTITY_TYPES`. `q` is a case-insensitive contains over `actorName`, `action` and `entityLabel`. `from` and `to` are UTC days, both included.

post.description: The server makes the group a `b2b` group (the storefront retail group cannot be created) and puts it last in the order. `discountPercent` is plain decimal text from 0 to 100 with at most two decimals; the money fields are `Money` of 0 or more. A group with `earnThreshold` 0 is never a promotion target; `depositLimit` 0 means no per-deposit limit. `isDefault: true` takes the default mark off the old default group in the same transaction. Fields left out are 0 or false. A name that another group already has (case-insensitive) is `422` on `name`.

get.description: One object, every section from one snapshot, cached about 15 seconds per (`scope`, `days`) (the sidebar reads it every minute for its counts). `scope` is `all`, `b2b` (merchants) or `b2c` (the storefront); `days` is 1, 7 or 14. `stats` covers orders created in the rolling window; `previous` is the window of the same length before it, or `null` when it had no order. `attention` is every item ranked critical, high, medium, low (stable): `supplier_down` and `supplier_degraded` come only from a real down or degraded check, never from an unknown or missing one, and supplier items only for active suppliers. Each kind has its own fixed severity (RULES dashboard 3): `disputes_due` counts every dispute that needs a response and is critical when the first is due within 3 days; `orders_review` counts merchant orders only (a held storefront order is `orders_held`); `fx_stale` uses the currencies page rule (older than 24 hours). `queues` has one row per service type; `pastSla` is the one age-only rule shared with `GET /admin/orders?pastSla=true`. `suppliers` maps the latest check to `up`, `degraded`, `down`, and an unknown or missing check to `degraded`. `services_below_floor` is judged on the effective cost (user rule 9). Money is USD as a 4-decimal string; payments, refunds and disputes convert per row at the checkout's locked rate or the current currency rate and the sum is rounded once. `storefront` and `topCustomers` are `null` for `b2b`, `revenueByChannel` is `null` unless `scope=all`; `storefront` always covers the last 30 days and its funnel is the customers module's `storefrontFunnel(30)`.

The dispatch state stays, except `sent` with `resetReference`, which becomes `needs_attention`; with `dispatch: true` it becomes `pending` and the job is queued in the same transaction. Neither `supplierId` nor `resetReference: true` is `422` on `supplierId`; the same supplier without a reset is a `204` with no event.

post.description: Approves a top-up and credits the wallet in one transaction: the money event `deposit` (Dr bank for a manual gateway or gateway_clearing for an automatic one, Cr client_wallet net, Cr fee_income fee, idempotency key `deposit:payment:<id>`), the linked invoice becomes paid, `invoice.paid` is queued for the merchant webhook, and the decision is audited. Only a pending top-up can be decided, and only when its gateway is manual or the payment was sent to review (`409 PAYMENT_AUTO_CREDIT_PENDING` otherwise: an automatic gateway credits by itself after the gateway check). A decided payment is `409 PAYMENT_ALREADY_REVIEWED`. An order (storefront) payment is `404`. Approving is `409 CONFLICT` when the gateway confirmed another amount or currency than the invoice (reject it and adjust the wallet by hand), when the gateway event can no longer be read, or when the invoice is no longer open. The answer's `client.walletBalance` already includes the credit.

post.description: Rejects a top-up with the reason the merchant sees: the payment becomes rejected with the reason as its note, the linked top-up invoice is voided (a staff-issued manual invoice stays open: the merchant may upload another receipt), nothing is posted to the ledger, and the decision is audited. Only a pending top-up can be decided, and only when its gateway is manual or the payment was sent to review (`409 PAYMENT_AUTO_CREDIT_PENDING` otherwise: an automatic gateway credits by itself after the gateway check). A decided payment is `409 PAYMENT_ALREADY_REVIEWED`. An order (storefront) payment is `404`. Approving is `409 CONFLICT` when the gateway confirmed another amount or currency than the invoice (reject it and adjust the wallet by hand), when the gateway event can no longer be read, or when the invoice is no longer open.

get.description: The price one merchant pays for one service, with the steps that led to it, in the order of the demo: client override, group service price, base price, the pricing rule (id `category`, label "Service rule", "Category rule" or "Global rule" by the winning rule), the group discount, then the optional `rounding` step. post.description: Works out the new base price of every service in the scope (`serviceIds` wins over `categoryId`; archived services are left out) and saves nothing, so it writes no audit entry (it is a POST only because the change travels in the body). `percent` gives `round(old x (1 + value / 100), 2)`, `fixed` gives `round(old + value, 2)`, half-up. `belowFloor` per line is the new price under the service floor (no merchant: rules for every group only) and the top-level `belowFloor` counts them. `422` on `amount` for zero, text that is not a number, or a new price that would not be above zero (the message names the service); `422` on `scope` when neither a category nor a non-empty `serviceIds` is sent.

post.description: One entry per pasted or uploaded line. Each is trimmed. A line shorter than 6 or longer than 128 characters, or with whitespace or a control character inside, is counted in `rejected` (not an error). A code that repeats an earlier line of the batch, or matches a code that is not void of any service, is counted in `duplicates`. The rest is stored encrypted (AES-GCM) with a keyed hash and the last four characters; a clear code is never logged or returned. `batchRef` (1 to 40 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`) names the batch; without it one is generated (`B-0031`). post.description: Runs the supplier-sync job (the worker calls `imeiservicelist` and `accountinfo`) and answers its counts. The API waits up to `timeoutMs` + 5 s: a supplier failure is `409 SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE`; a wait that runs out while the job goes on is `504 SUPPLIER_TIMEOUT`. A paused supplier may sync; a disabled one is `409 SUPPLIER_DISABLED`. The sync updates `supplier_services` (a changed credit sets `price_changed_at`; a service no longer listed becomes unavailable), recomputes the effective cost of every linked service and moves the catalog price version.

post.description: The Dhru Fusion v6.1 compatible endpoint (decision 026): `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object) as a form body (`multipart/form-data` and JSON are accepted too). Eight actions: `accountinfo`, `imeiservicelist`, `placeimeiorder`, `placeimeiorderbulk`, `getimeiorder`, `getimeiorderbulk`, `placefileorder` and `getfileorder`. Every answer is HTTP 200 with the headers `X-Powered-By: DHRU-FUSION` and `dhru-fusion-api-version: 6.1` and the body `{ "SUCCESS": [ ... ], "apiversion": "6.1" }` or `{ "ERROR": [ { "MESSAGE": "..." } ], "apiversion": "6.1" }`; a bulk action answers `{ "<request id>": { "SUCCESS" | "ERROR": [ ... ] }, ..., "apiversion": "6.1" }`. A wrong credential is "Authentication Failed", an unknown action "Invalid Action". The key must carry the `dhru` scope; the allowed addresses and the per-minute limit of the key apply.

oneOf.title: accountinfo
oneOf.description: Account info. The merchant's available balance (`credit`: the wallet balance plus the credit limit), email and currency. The key `AccoutInfo` is spelled as in the Dhru Fusion standard.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: This action takes no parameters.

credit.description: What the merchant may spend now: balance plus credit limit.

oneOf.title: imeiservicelist
oneOf.description: IMEI service list. The IMEI, server and remote services the merchant may order, grouped by category, at its own price (`CREDIT`), with the quantity rules and the custom fields (`Requires.Custom`). File services are not listed. Archived and disabled services and categories the merchant's group may not see are never listed. Every price shown is remembered as the merchant's listed price (user rule 9).

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: This action takes no parameters.

QNT.description: `1` when the service sells more than one quantity.

QNTOPTIONS.description: The packs a service sells, comma separated; `""` when it sells a range.

type.description: `serviceimei`, `serviceserver` or `serviceremote`.

fieldname.description: The field key: the name `CUSTOMFIELD` takes.

fieldoptions.description: The choices of a dropdown, comma separated; `""` otherwise.

oneOf.title: placeimeiorder
oneOf.description: Place an IMEI, server or remote order. Orders a service at the merchant's own price and holds it from the wallet. `ID` is the `SERVICEID` of `imeiservicelist`; an IMEI service takes `IMEI`, a server or remote service its custom fields in `CUSTOMFIELD`. The answer is immediate: `REFERENCEID` is our order id (status 0). A price that rose more than the tolerance above the price last listed is refused with "Price changed. Please refresh the service list and order again."; a balance that is too low with "Not enough credits". A File service is placed with `placefileorder`.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

QNT.description: The quantity; defaults to the service's minimum.

post.description: Orders a service at the merchant's own price (the one price resolver). The price is held from the wallet in the same transaction; an order that would cost more than the tolerance above the price the merchant last listed is refused (`PRICE_CHANGED`, with both prices), a smaller raise is charged and recorded; a second open order for the same service and input is refused under the service's `block_open` rule (`DUPLICATE_ORDER`). An IMEI service takes `imei` (15 digits, Luhn) or `imeis` (a bulk of up to 100: one order each, all placed or none); a server or remote service takes `inputs`; a File service a `fileId` and/or `inputs`. The answer is immediate: the orders are `pending`, in the manual queue or waiting for the dispatch job.

imei.description: The IMEI of an IMEI service.

imeis.description: A bulk order: one order of the same service per IMEI, placed all together or not at all.

inputs.description: The values of the service's custom fields by field key (`GET /client/services/:id`).

fileId.description: The uploaded input file of a File service.

id.description: The order id, also the Dhru REFERENCEID.

imei.description: The order's main input; `''` when it has none.

unitPrice.description: Decimal string with exactly 4 fraction digits.

post.description: Orders a service at the merchant's own price (the one price resolver). The price is held from the wallet in the same transaction. An order that would cost more than the tolerance above the price the merchant last listed is refused with `409 PRICE_CHANGED` (`listedPrice` and `currentPrice` in the body: list the services again and order again), a smaller raise is charged and recorded. A second open order for the same service and input is refused under the service's `block_open` rule (`DUPLICATE_ORDER`). An IMEI service takes `imei` (15 digits, Luhn); a server or remote service takes `inputs`; a File service a `fileId` and/or `inputs`. The answer is immediate: the order is `pending` (or already `completed` when the service delivers from stock). Send an `Idempotency-Key` so that a retry never places a second order. Scope `orders:write`.

post.description: Places up to 100 orders in one request, each item exactly as `POST /v1/orders` would (the price, the price guard, the duplicate rule, the hold). The answer has one result per item, in the order sent: `ok: true` with the order, or `ok: false` with the refusal (`code`, `status`, `detail`, field `errors`, and `listedPrice` and `currentPrice` for a changed price). An item that is refused places nothing and never stops the others; the items draw on one wallet in the order sent, so a later item may be refused for lack of funds. The answer is `200` even when every item was refused. An `Idempotency-Key` stores the whole answer and replays it.

get.description: The services the merchant may order, at the price it pays (client price, else group price, else the base price after the pricing rule, the group discount, rounding and the floor), in id order, in pages: `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `cursor` (the `nextCursor` of the previous page). Filters: `type`, `categoryId`; `q` is a case-insensitive contains over name, code and category. Archived and disabled services and categories the merchant's group may not see are never listed. Every price shown is remembered as the merchant's listed price: an order that costs much more than the price last shown is refused with `PRICE_CHANGED` (user rule 9). Scope `services:read`.

post.description: A payment gateway confirms a top-up. The delivery must carry the gateway's signature (the scheme of its driver), a signed time within 5 minutes of now and an event id not seen before; otherwise `400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. A confirmed payment of an open invoice is recorded once (the gateway reference is unique): the payment waits `payments.auto_credit_delay_minutes` (at least the gateway hold hours), then a job asks the gateway again and credits the wallet. A repeat of the same event answers `200` and changes nothing. Events billing does not use are acknowledged with `200`.

apiKey.description: Merchant API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key has scopes (each operation names the one it needs), an optional list of allowed IP addresses and its own requests-per-minute limit.

capabilityToken.description: An unguessable token in the path (checkout, order tracking, support ticket or sign-in link) that authorises exactly one record. Sent by email or shown once; stored only as a hash.

customerSession.name: gsm_store_session
customerSession.description: Storefront customer session cookie, set by the sign-in routes under `/store/v1/auth` (password or sign-in link). HttpOnly; carries the `__Host-` prefix in production. Requests that change data also send `X-CSRF-Token`.

dhruCredentials.description: Dhru Fusion credentials are not an HTTP header: send `username` and `apiaccesskey` as form fields in the request body. The key must carry the `dhru` scope and passes the same IP and rate-limit checks as a REST v1 key.

gatewaySignature.description: Payment gateway webhook, verified per gateway with its signing secret. Deliveries outside a 5-minute window are refused and events are de-duplicated by the gateway event id.

merchantSession.name: gsm_client_session
merchantSession.description: Merchant portal session cookie, set by the sign-in routes under `/client/auth`. HttpOnly; carries the `__Host-` prefix in production. Requests that change data also send `X-CSRF-Token`.

metricsAccess.description: Prometheus scrape access: loopback and private networks, or `Authorization: Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN>`. When a token is configured it is required from every caller.

staffSession.name: gsm_admin_session
staffSession.description: Staff session cookie, set by the sign-in steps under `/admin/auth` (password, then the 2FA code). HttpOnly; carries the `__Host-` prefix in production. Requests that change data also send the `X-CSRF-Token` header returned by sign-in. The permission a route needs is shown in `x-gsm-permission`.

urlSecret.description: A secret path segment (for example `/webhooks/telegram/{secret}`) that only the provider knows; a wrong secret answers as if the route did not exist.

webhookSignature.name: X-GSM-Signature
webhookSignature.description: Header we add to every outgoing webhook event: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">`, keyed with the secret of the webhook endpoint. Recompute it over the raw body and refuse deliveries older than 5 minutes. Documented for receivers; it cannot be used to call this API.
